ecological_hypothesis: Persistent physical site template contributes to long-run differences among Thalassia transects; measured depth and sediment should explain held-out node-level state beyond broad bay identity and coordinates.

outcome_construction.aggregation: mean annual state within node over all available years

physical_template.sediment_conflict_rule: Use only point events with exactly one normalized sediment label; the 39 preflight conflict events are excluded.

validation: leave-one-node-out; each stable transect is predicted once from all other eligible nodes

scoring.primary_cross_outcome_rule: Measured site template is considered broadly supported only if it passes the support rule for at least 2 of the 3 primary occurrence/abundance outcomes.

interpretation_map.supported: Depth/sediment recover generalizable persistent site-state information beyond water-body identity and coordinates.
interpretation_map.unsupported: The strong node effect remains largely unresolved by depth/sediment alone; prioritize benthic light, hydrodynamics, chronic local water quality, and meadow/clonal legacy.
interpretation_map.mixed: Measured template explains some state dimensions but not a general persistent-site effect.

claim_boundary: Retrospective cross-node ecological analysis, not causal identification.
Depth summaries include tidal/sampling variation and are not exact bathymetry.
Sediment data are not focal-taxon selected but their availability depends on the biological record structure.
A positive result would not prove depth or sediment causes persistence; a negative result would not rule out site-template ecology.
Do not alter the minimum-year rule, feature set, learner, or support threshold after opening the outcome result.
